correctness.rationale: The image of a generated subalgebra in the central quotient is the span of the two images. If the images span, two lifts have nonzero bracket by nondegeneracy, forcing the center into the generated algebra, including in characteristic two. Subalgebras containing the center are in bijection with all subspaces; those avoiding it are graphs of functionals on totally isotropic spaces. Counting ordered isotropic bases successively gives q^(2n-i)-q^i possibilities at step i, divided by the number of ordered bases of the target rank. After multiplying by q^r for the graph functional, the bound is Phi_infty^-1 q^(2nr-3r(r-1)/2). Maximizing and dividing by the central count, at least q^(n^2), gives the stated exceptional-population bound, and conditioning on both containing the center gives the factor-2 probability comparison. For dimensions n+j and n+k, choosing the intersection of dimension j+k and a graph in the quotient by that intersection gives the exact count and the displayed conditional kernel, zero if j+k<0. In the central range |j|<=n/2, the unnormalized rank probability weight is q^(-j^2)(1/Phi_infty+O_q(q^(-n/2))); the weighted errors, not unweighted errors times the number of ranks, are summable. The omitted mass is O_q(q^(-n^2/4)), and the conditional kernel is uniformly within O_q(q^(-n/2)) of its limit on the central range. This proves the rate after normalizing and multiplying the two rank weights. Positive limiting weights occur both on possible and impossible spanning sizes, so the constant is strictly between zero and one.
residual_risks: The uploaded checker was inspected but not executed; 12 finite comparisons under its loose tolerance alone would not certify the rate. Independent enumerations used prime fields only; the proof, not the computation, includes extension fields.
The rate is for n tending to infinity with q fixed.

value.rationale: Uniform choice across the entire subalgebra lattice is a natural sampling law, inequivalent to a fixed dimension. The result explains why the generation limit exists without degenerating to zero or one: the quotient ranks stay within a bounded window, fluctuations there affect the spanning kernel, and noncentral picks have negligible population. The explicit theta mixture and quantitative transfer are useful beyond a finite census of this algebra family.
residual_risks: No extension to larger-center algebras, changing field size or other sampling models is asserted.
